scenes.headline: Most of an 8-Hour Day Isn't Real Work
bullets: News sites and social media ate the most time
scenes.narration: A survey of nearly two thousand UK office workers found they were truly productive for just two hours and fifty-three minutes a day. Grinding for eight hours does not mean working for eight hours.
scenes.source: Vouchercloud survey of 1,989 UK office workers (2016)

scenes.headline: Work in ~90-Minute Blocks
scenes.left_body: Checking your phone mid-task breaks focus that takes time to rebuild
scenes.narration: Sleep researcher Nathaniel Kleitman proposed a roughly ninety-minute rest and activity cycle that keeps running while we are awake. So work in focused blocks of about ninety minutes, then take a real break.

scenes.headline: 3 Blocks a Week = 234 Hours a Year
scenes.stat_subtext: Enough to launch 52 videos or a profitable digital business
scenes.narration: Protect just one phone-free ninety-minute block three mornings a week, and you get back two hundred thirty hours of pure creation a year, more than enough to change your life.
scenes.source: Calculation: 3 x 90 min x 52 weeks = 234 hours
